SELECT airport_iata, category, item, value, unit, status, effective_from, effective_to FROM curated_constraint WHERE airport_iata IN ('LAX','SNA') ORDER BY airport_iata, category, item

SELECT * FROM dim_airport WHERE oa_iata IN ('LAX','SNA')

answer.headline: LAX schedules a higher peak hour than SNA and has a higher tight-capacity passenger share, on a larger and longer runway plant
answer.body: Over {F40.period}, Los Angeles International (LAX) and John Wayne Orange County in Santa Ana (SNA) differ on both requested measures. The scheduled peak-hour rate is {F40} at LAX and {F41} at SNA (LAX minus SNA {F42}, ratio {F43}). The busiest scheduled hour is {F5} at LAX and {F6} at SNA (difference {F13}, ratio {F14}). Tight-capacity passenger share is {F7} at LAX and {F8} at SNA (share difference {F15}, relative difference {F16}). Open runways are {F9} at LAX and {F10} at SNA (difference {F46}, ratio {F21}). Percentile peak per open runway is {F44} at LAX and {F45} at SNA, so that ratio is {F53} rather than {F43}. Exploratory dimension figures put the longest runway at {F27} feet at LAX and {F34} feet at SNA, and the long-runway count at {F28} versus {F35}. These peaks are domestic reporting-carrier lower bounds: On-Time coverage of airline departures is {F36} at LAX and {F37} at SNA.

claims.text: During {F40.period}, the scheduled peak-hour percentile rate is {F40} at LAX and {F41} at SNA. The difference is {F42} and the LAX-to-SNA ratio is {F43}.
The busiest scheduled hour in the same window is {F5} at LAX and {F6} at SNA. The difference is {F13} and the ratio is {F14}.
Using {F7.label}, the tight-capacity passenger share is {F7} at LAX and {F8} at SNA. The difference in shares is {F15}. Relative to SNA, the LAX share is higher by {F16}.
The catalog open-runway count is {F9} at LAX and {F10} at SNA. The difference is {F46} and the ratio is {F21}.

Exploratory airport-dimension figures, not catalog metrics, show a longest runway of {F27} feet at LAX and {F34} feet at SNA (difference {F47} feet, ratio {F48}). The long-runway count ({F28.label}) is {F28} at LAX and {F35} at SNA (difference {F49}).

Percentile peak divided by open runways is {F44} at LAX and {F45} at SNA (difference {F54}, ratio {F53}). Busiest scheduled hour divided by open runways is {F19} at LAX and {F20} at SNA (difference {F55}, ratio {F52}).
On-Time coverage of airline departures is {F36} at LAX and {F37} at SNA (LAX minus SNA {F50}). International seat share is {F38} at LAX and {F39} at SNA (difference {F51}).

Scaling the scheduled peak by the open-runway count narrows the LAX-to-SNA percentile ratio from {F43} to {F53}, and the busiest-hour ratio from {F14} to {F52}. Runway count therefore does not account for the whole peak gap. This ratio is a normalization, not a measured runway-utilization or acceptance rate. The runways are also unequal in length: the longest-runway ratio is {F48} and the long-runway-count difference is {F49}.

Because On-Time coverage is lower at LAX by {F50} and international seat share is higher at LAX by {F51}, the scheduled-peak comparison leaves out a larger share of LAX flying than of SNA flying. The amount by which international and non-reporting flights would raise the LAX peak is not established.

assumptions: Santa Ana is bound to John Wayne Orange County International Airport (SNA). LAX is bound to Los Angeles International Airport, not the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim group that also contains SNA.
Flow metrics share the window {F40.period}. Open-runway counts are the static catalog snapshot. Longest-runway and long-runway counts are exploratory reads of the airport dimension.
Tight-capacity passenger share uses the catalog default threshold, as named in {F7.label}.
Per-runway figures divide a scheduled-peak statistic by the count of open runways only. They do not adjust for length, dependence between runways, or hours the airport may operate.
limitations: Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured. Tight-capacity passenger share is the share of departing passengers on route-months above a seat-factor threshold. That seat factor is not, by itself, evidence of unmet demand.

Geometric runway configuration — orientation, parallel versus intersecting layout, centerline separation, and independent arrival rates — is not available for this pair. Modeled hourly runway throughput is not a numeric finding for both airports, so the scheduled peak was not compared with a published acceptance rate.
A peak per long runway is not defined for SNA because that count is {F35}.
Scheduled peak operations cover domestic flights of reporting carriers only and are a lower bound on total scheduled operations.
Open-runway counts are a static snapshot and are not guaranteed to match the traffic window {F40.period}.
This is a descriptive comparison of two airports in the same metro area. It is not an investment screen and not a valuation.
